title: Per-SLO Signal Fusion and Progressive Evacuation Runbook for Cross-Region Degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe recurring noisy paging during partial capacity degradation in a single region even when global SLOs remain nominal. Existing suppression rules are per-alert and threshold-based, which leads to either too much noise (false positives) or missed early degradation signs. Goals: 1) Create a fused "evacuation score" that combines SLI trends (latency p95/p99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, queueing depth, KV cache hit-rate), regional error-rate multipliers, and synthetic canary health into a single probabilistic signal. 2) Implement a progressive evacuation strategy that (a) initiates soft load-shedding and traffic shaping within region at low scores, (b) ramps circuit-breakers and divert traffic to standby regions at medium scores, and (c) trigger cross-region cutover and stricter shedding at high scores. 3) Integrate score-based pager severity adjustments to reduce noisy P0 pages when the fused signal indicates low global impact. 4) Automate key runbook steps for on-call (contextual checks, automated mitigations, safe rollback). Acceptance criteria: - Evacuation score defined and calculated in prod telemetry pipeline (Grafana dashboard) with <10s aggregation latency. - Pager volume for region-degradation incidents reduced by >=40% in first 30 days post-rollout with no increase in customer-visible errors. - Automated first-responder mitigations (prefix cache flush, adaptive batching reduce, model variant fallback) execute reliably in canary and reduce token latency by measurable amount. - Playbook clearly documents prechecks, escalation paths, and rollback. Implementation plan: - Telemetry: add fused score computation Lambda (serving-telemetry) + new metrics (evac_score, evac_phase) to metrics API. - Routing: implement phased shedding hooks in routing-proxy and runtime to accept evac_phase and apply token-bucket rate limits and model-variant fallbacks. - Circuit breakers: hysteresis windows per region with exponential backoff and recovery probes. - Runbook/Automation: author structured runbook in Confluence with automated runbook steps implemented as orchestrator playbooks (orchestration service PR). Rollout: alpha canary in staging -> canary in us-west-2 with synthetic canaries -> gradual rollout to beta regions -> global. Metrics and dashboards: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/evac/evac-score-overview, synthetic dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/synth/latency-canaries. Links: Confluence runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/EVAC+Runbook, design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EvacDesign, github PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/7421, https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proxy/pull/1984. Risks & trade-offs: - Overly aggressive fusion can suppress genuine high-impact incidents; mitigated via conservative thresholds and a manual override in console. - Cross-region cutover increases cost; default policy will bias to regional mitigation first. Dependencies: routing-proxy feature flag, telemetry pipeline windowing improvement, oncall notifications experiment (PM-4012).
